chunks: And in the hadith of Malik ibn Ayn, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) encouraged the people at Siffin.

So he said: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, pointed you to a trade that will save you from a painful punishment and heal you with the goodness of belief in Allah and striving in the way of Allah, and made its reward forgiveness of sin and goodly dwellings in the Gardens of Eden.
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Indeed Allah loves those who fight in His cause in rows as if they were a solid structure.' So align your rows like a solid structure.

So place the armored in front and the unarmored behind, and grit your teeth for it is stronger for the swords upon the heads, and be quick in launching the sides of the spears for it is more violent for the spikes, and lower your eyes for it is linked to composure and tranquility for the hearts, and deaden your voices for it drives out failure and is closer to dignity.

And do not incline your flags nor let them fall, and do not make them with anyone except your bravest ones, for the defenders of honor and the patient during the descent of realities, they are the protecting people.

And do not mutilate the killed ones, and when you arrive to the men of the people, do not tear down a veil, nor enter a house, and do not take anything from their wealth except what you find among their soldiers.

And do not agitate a woman with harm. And if they insult your honor and swear at your leaders and your righteous ones, so (it is because) they are weak of strength, soul, and intellect. And we have been ordered with restraining from them, and they were polytheist women.
And if a man had grabbed the woman, he would be reproached for it, and his posterity from after him.
And know that the defenders are those who surround their flags, encompass them, and go by their sides, behind them, and in front of them.
And they do not lose it; they do not stay back from it so as to surrender it, nor do they move ahead of it so as to isolate it.

May Allah have mercy on a man who consoles his brother by himself and does not leave his pair to his brother, so his pair and his brother's pair meet, and he acquires blame and becomes lowly through that.
And how can he not be like that, while he is fighting as two, and this one restrains his hand, having left his pair upon his brother fleeing from him looking at him, and this one.
So the one who does it, Allah will abhor him. Therefore, do not expose yourselves to the loathing of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For indeed your passage is to Allah.
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: 'Fleeing will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will not enjoy except for a little while.'

And I swear by Allah, if you flee from the swords of the present, you will not be safe from the swords of the future. So seek assistance with patience and truthfulness, for indeed victory descends after patience.
So strive in Allah the way He deserves, and there is no strength except with Allah.

And he (peace be upon him) said when he passed by a flag of the people of Syria whose owners were not moving from their places: 'Indeed they will not move from their places without a thrust that extracts the soul, and a strike that splits the head and breaks the bones, and the wrists and palms fall off.'
Until their foreheads are cracked with the force of iron, and their eyelids scatter upon their chests and chins. Where are the people of patience and seekers of reward?
So a band of Muslims marched to him, and its right wing returned to its place and its center wing, and exposed those facing them. So he returned until he ended up to them.
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'I have seen your visitation and your retreating from your ranks, giving an opportunity to the unjust and the tyrants, and the Bedouins of the people of Syria.'
And you are the top ones of the Arabs, the great peak, and enduring ones of the night by the recitation of the Quran and the callers from the people of the Truth when the erroneous go astray.

Had it not been for your facing them after your turning your backs on them, and your regrouping after your retreating, there would have obligated upon you what gets obligated upon the turner of his back on the day of the battle, and you would be in what I view as the destroyed ones.

And it has comforted me part of what I find, and healed part of the concerns of my chest, when I saw you defeating them just as they had defeated you, and you dislodged them from their rows just as they had dislodged you.
And you were striking them with the swords to the extent that their first ones rode upon their last ones like the driven camel.
Now, so be patient. Tranquility has descended upon you, and Allah will affirm you with conviction.

And the defeated one should know that he has angered his Lord and destroyed himself. Indeed in fleeing is the fury of Allah, and the humiliation that is necessitated, and the remaining stigma, and spoiling of the life over it.
And the fleer is without an increase in his age, and there is no barrier between him and his day, nor would his Lord be pleased with him.
And for a death to come to the man before he indulges in these characteristics is better than the pleasure of being clothed by them and agreeing over them.
And in another speech of his: 'And when you meet these people tomorrow, do not fight them until they fight you. So when they initiate with you, then break them down.'

And upon you be tranquility and dignity, and grit your teeth for it is strength for the swords on the heads, and lower your eyes, and keep your eyes upon the foreheads of the cavalry horses and the faces of the men.

And minimize your speech for it drives away failure and removes the rush, and resign yourselves to dueling, confrontation, and argumentation, and be steadfast and mention Allah, Mighty and Majestic, frequently.
For the defenders of honor during the descent of realities are the protecting people who surround their flags and strike around their sides and in front of them.
And when you carry it, do the deed of one man, and upon you be being protective, for war is a competition.
They do not attack you with an attack after a fleeing, nor an advance after a retreat.
And the one who throws to you for peace, accept it from him, and seek assistance with patience, for after patience is victory from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
Indeed the earth is Allah's; He causes His servants to inherit it as He wills, and the end is for those who are pious.
ai.seo_question: What were the key military and ethical instructions given by Imam Ali (AS) at the Battle of Siffin?
ai.summary: This passage from *Al-Kafi* records Imam Ali’s (as) comprehensive military address at Siffin, blending tactical instructions—such as maintaining formation and protecting the flag—with spiritual discipline like *sakinah* (tranquility) and *sabr* (patience). It highlights the Shia emphasis on *adab al-harb* (etiquette of war), prohibiting mutilation and ensuring the flag remains with the brave, while linking battlefield conduct directly to divine favor and victory.
